mainTopic: Undoing vows: mistaken vows, a פתח from Torah commandments, and a פתח from the wife's כתובה
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. רבי אבא quotes a later משנה about a נדר טעות (a mistaken vow) and asks why, according to רבי יוחנן, the משנה would teach the same law twice. The גמרא admits this is a real difficulty (קשיא). Next comes a new משנה with another way to open a vow (פתח), from רבי מאיר: the חכם asks the vower whether he would have vowed had he known he was breaking Torah commandments like 'Do not take revenge' and 'Love your neighbor', and that he can no longer help a poor fellow Jew. The גמרא asks why the vower can't simply give through the community charity fund. The answer is that a person sliding into poverty first needs private help, before he ever reaches the charity collector. Another משנה then teaches that a vow can be opened by pointing to the wife's כתובה, with a story about a man whom רבי עקיבא made pay the full כתובה 'even if you sell the hair on your head.' The גמרא explains that the כתובה was paid from land, and the hair was what he would sell afterward for food. It then asks whether this proves a debtor is not left his basic needs, and רב נחמן בר רבי יצחק begins to answer. His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Rabbi Abba quotes a later משנה about a mistaken vow
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא begins an objection by quoting a later משנה: someone who vows not to marry a woman because she is 'ugly,' 'black,' or 'short,' when in fact she is not, may marry her, because the vow was a mistake from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא objected: If a man says, 'It is קונם that I will not marry this ugly woman,' but she is really beautiful; or 'this black woman,' but she is really white; or 'this short woman,' but she is really tall, he may marry her. This is not because she changed. It is because the vow was a mistake from the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא is setting up a challenge by quoting a later משנה about a נדר טעות. The attack itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted משנה stresses that the woman never changed. The vow was simply based on wrong facts from the start. This sets up the point that the משנה already teaches the law of a mistaken vow in a separate place.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from a משנה or ברייתא
A word used to make a vow, meaning 'forbidden to me like a קרבן'
A mistaken vow, made based on wrong facts, so it was never valid
He is permitted to her (he may marry her)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba raised an objection:
"Konam that I will not marry ugly so-and-so,"
and in fact she is beautiful.
"Black," and in fact she is white.
"Short," and in fact she is tall —
he is permitted to her.
Not because she was ugly and became beautiful,
black and became white,
short and became tall —
but rather because the vow was a mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an objection against רבי יוחנן's reading of the previous משנה, discussed just before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that the earlier משנה is a case of נדר טעות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A later משנה already teaches נדר טעות, so the earlier משנה would be repeating the same law.

steps.title: Why would the משנה teach a mistaken vow twice?
steps.stepSummary: For רב הונא, the two משניות teach two different laws. For רבי יוחנן, both would be about נדר טעות, so one of them would be extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רב הונא, who said the earlier case is like someone who hangs his vow on a condition. Then one משנה teaches a vow hanging on a condition, and the other teaches a mistaken vow. But for רבי יוחנן, who said the earlier case is where the dog had already died or the person had already repented, why would the משנה need to teach a mistaken vow twice?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא now makes his attack. If רבי יוחנן is right, the משנה would be repeating itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא reads the earlier משנה as a תולה נדרו בדבר, a vow that depends on a condition that later changed. That is a different law from a mistaken vow, so no repeat. רבי יוחנן says the facts had already changed before the vow was made, which makes it a mistaken vow, the same law as the later משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for... (one view fits; a 'but' for the other view is coming)
Hangs his vow on a matter, so the vow depends on a condition
Two times
Why do I need...? (Why is this extra teaching needed?)

steps.confusionAlert: Both רב הונא and רבי יוחנן are explaining רבי מאיר's ruling in the earlier משנה that the vow is undone. They disagree on WHY: a vow that depends on a condition (רב הונא) or a vow that was mistaken from the start (רבי יוחנן). The challenge is only about the משנה repeating itself.

phrases.english: It works well according to Rav Huna,
who said he is considered like one who hangs his vow on a matter:
[the Mishnah] taught one who hangs his vow on a matter,
phrases.notes: That's the earlier משנה: a vow not to enter a house because a bad dog is inside, or not to marry a woman because her father is bad.

phrases.english: and it taught a mistaken vow.
But according to Rabbi Yochanan,
who said [the dog] had already died
or [the person] had already repented,
why do I need [the Mishnah] to teach
a mistaken vow two times?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב הוּנָא דְּאָמַר נַעֲשָׂה כְּתוֹלֶה נִדְרוֹ בְּדָבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה quoted in step 1 to attack רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's explanation of the earlier משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה does not teach the same law twice. Under רבי יוחנן, both משניות teach נדר טעות, so one is extra.

steps.title: The challenge stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא closes with 'קשיא': the question against רבי יוחנן remains difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer to רבי אבא's challenge and leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' means the question stands, but רבי יוחנן's view is not thrown out completely. That would be 'תיובתא'. It just stays a real difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult. The question is left without an answer, but the view is not fully rejected.

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא and רבי יוחנן explain the earlier משנה differently. רבי יוחנן's reading is left with an unanswered difficulty, because it makes the משנה teach נדר טעות twice.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' is weaker than 'תיובתא'. With קשיא the opinion still stands. We just don't have an answer to the question.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the challenge from step 2 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge against רבי יוחנן stays unresolved.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: opening a vow with Torah commandments
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר teaches that a חכם can undo a vow by asking the vower whether he realized his vow makes him break commandments like 'Do not take revenge,' 'Do not bear a grudge,' 'Do not hate your brother,' 'Love your neighbor,' and 'Your brother shall live with you,' since he can no longer help support a poor man. If the vower says he would not have vowed had he known, the vow is undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר also said: They can open a way to undo the vow from what is written in the Torah. They say to him: 'Had you known that you are breaking "Do not take revenge," "Do not bear a grudge," "Do not hate your brother in your heart," "Love your neighbor as yourself," and "Your brother shall live with you," since he is poor and you cannot support him...' If he answers, 'Had I known it was so, I would not have vowed,' the vow is undone.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives another way, a פתח, for a חכם to undo a vow. He points out the Torah commandments the vower is now breaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Vowing not to let a fellow Jew benefit from you can be an act of revenge, a grudge, or hatred. It also stops you from helping him if he is poor. If the vower honestly says he would never have vowed had he thought about this, the vow is treated as made without full awareness, so it can be undone.

keyTerms.meaning: They open, meaning they find a 'פתח', an opening to undo the vow
Do not take revenge (ויקרא 19:18)
Do not bear a grudge (ויקרא 19:18)
Your brother shall live with you, a מצוה to help support a fellow Jew (ויקרא 25:36)
To support him, to provide him a living

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the Torah's commandments about how we treat others can be used as a real reason to undo a vow that hurts another person.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
And Rabbi Meir further said:
They may open for him from what is written in the Torah,
phrases.notes: 'Open' means open a way to undo his vow.

phrases.english: and they say to him:
Had you known
that you are transgressing "You shall not take revenge,"
phrases.notes: This verse and the next three are ויקרא 19:17–18.

phrases.english: and "You shall not bear a grudge,"
and "You shall not hate your brother in your heart,"
"And you shall love your neighbor as yourself,"
"And your brother shall live with you,"
since he is poor
and you are not able to support him.
If he said: Had I known
that it is so, I would not have vowed —
then it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר פּוֹתְחִין לוֹ מִן הַכָּתוּב שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. It moves on from the mistaken-vow discussion to a new kind of פתח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow can be undone by showing the vower that it makes him break Torah commandments between people, if he says he would not have vowed had he known.

steps.title: Can't the vower say the poor man is the community's job?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר רב קטינא asks: the vower could answer that not every poor person is his personal duty. He will give his share to the community fund, and that will support this poor man too. So the last point in the משנה should not work as a פתח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר רב קטינא said to the רבנן: Let the vower say, 'Not everyone who becomes poor falls on me. Whatever part of his support reaches me, I will give together with everyone else.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the משנה's last point. Maybe the vower is not really stopping himself from supporting the poor man, since he can still give through the community fund.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's argument was that the vow blocks the vower from fulfilling 'וחי אחיך עמך'. רב הונא בר רב קטינא says this is not true. The vower can still pay his part through communal צדקה, which does not count as giving the man direct benefit. If so, the vower would not regret his vow, and this פתח should fail.

keyTerms.meaning: Who becomes poor
Does not fall on me, meaning it is not my personal responsibility
Together with everyone else
I will support

phrases.english: Gemara:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְהוּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא לְרַבָּנַן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Rav Ketina said to the Rabbis:
Let him say: Everyone who becomes poor
does not fall upon me.
Whatever reaches me to support him —
phrases.notes: He means his share of the community's charity, not a private gift.

phrases.english: together with everyone else I will support him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְהוּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר רַב קַטִּינָא לְרַבָּנַן נֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last argument in the משנה of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's claim that the vow stops the vower from fulfilling 'וחי אחיך עמך'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vower can still support the poor man through the community fund. So the vow does not really block this מצוה, and he has no reason to regret it.

steps.title: A falling person needs private help before reaching the charity fund
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן answer: a person who is falling into poverty does not go straight to the charity collector. First he needs private help to keep him from falling all the way. The vow blocks exactly that help.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: I say that anyone who falls does not fall into the hands of the charity collector first.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן defend the משנה. Before someone becomes a charity case, he first needs personal help from people around him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The community fund only helps once a person is already fully poor. In the early stage of falling, private support can keep him on his feet. The vow stops the vower from giving that help, so 'וחי אחיך עמך' really is blocked, and the פתח works.

keyTerms.meaning: They said to him
The one who falls, meaning into poverty
The charity collector who runs the community fund
First, at the beginning

steps.whatToRemember: A vow that stops you from helping someone in need can be undone by pointing to the Torah's מצוות between people. Communal צדקה does not replace the private help a person needs while he is first falling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a lasting idea about צדקה: the best help is catching someone early, before he must rely on public charity.

phrases.english: They said to him:
I say that anyone who falls,
does not fall into the hands of the charity collector first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ אֲנִי אוֹמֵר כׇּל הַנּוֹפֵל
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: shows the vow does block a real form of help
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vower can fulfill his duty to the poor man through the community fund, so the vow costs him nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person sliding into poverty first needs private help before he reaches the charity collector. The vow blocks this, so the פתח is valid.

steps.title: A vow can be opened with the wife's כתובה
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins: a חכם can open a way to undo a man's vow by pointing to his wife's כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They may open a way to undo a man's vow by bringing up his wife's כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts here with another type of פתח. The vower is reminded of the כתובה he would have to pay if his vow led to divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a vow would force a man to divorce his wife, he would have to pay her כתובה. Pointing this out may make him realize he would never have vowed. The next two steps show this with a story about רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: His wife's כתובה, the marriage contract money owed to her if they divorce

phrases.english: Mishnah:
They may open for a man with his wife's marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with another type of פתח, after the Torah-commandment פתח of steps 4–6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חכם may undo a vow by reminding the man of his wife's כתובה.

steps.title: A man vows against his wife and asks to pay only half her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells a story. A man vowed that his wife may not benefit from him, and her כתובה was 400 דינרים. רבי עקיבא ordered him to pay it. The man asked to pay only half.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story about a man who vowed that his wife could not benefit from him. Her כתובה was 400 דינרים. He came before רבי עקיבא, who told him to pay her the כתובה. The man said: 'רבי, my father left 800 דינרים. My brother took 400 and I took 400. Isn't it enough that she takes 200 and I keep 200?'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a real story to show how the כתובה can open a way to undo a vow. This step sets up the story. רבי עקיבא's answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow means he cannot stay married to her, so he has to pay her כתובה. Paying 400 would use up his whole inheritance, so he tries to split it with her. He has not yet seen how much the vow will cost him.

keyTerms.meaning: A story that really happened
Made a vow forbidding someone to benefit from him
The money a husband owes his wife if the marriage ends
Silver coins

phrases.english: And there was a story with a man who vowed that his wife may not benefit from him,
and her כתובה was four hundred דינרים.
And he came before רבי עקיבא,
and he obligated him to give her the כתובה.
He said to him: Rebbi,
my father left eight hundred דינרים.

phrases.aramaic: נָטַל אָחִי אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת, וַאֲנִי אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת.
phrases.english: My brother took four hundred, and I took four hundred.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא דַּיָּה שֶׁתִּטּוֹל הִיא מָאתַיִם וַאֲנִי מָאתַיִם?
phrases.english: Isn't it enough that she takes two hundred and I keep two hundred?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a story that shows the rule from step 7, that the כתובה can be used to undo a vow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא obligates the man to pay the full כתובה because of his vow.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא insists on full payment and the man regrets his vow
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says he must pay the full כתובה even if he has to sell the hair on his head. The man says he would never have vowed had he known, so רבי עקיבא undoes the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: 'Even if you have to sell the hair on your head, you must give her the full כתובה.' The man said: 'If I had known it was like this, I would not have vowed.' And רבי עקיבא undid the vow, so she was allowed to benefit from him again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא turns down the man's offer. Once the man sees the true cost of his vow, he regrets it, and רבי עקיבא undoes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the פתח in action: the man learns something he did not think about when he vowed, which is that he must pay the whole כתובה. Because he says he would not have vowed had he known, the vow can be undone.

keyTerms.meaning: The hair on your head
If I had known
And he undid the vow, so she was allowed again

steps.whatToRemember: The story shows that the money he must pay for the כתובה can be the opening (פתח) that undoes the vow.

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא said to him:
Even if you have to sell the hair on your head,
you must give her the full כתובה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אִילּוּ הָיִיתִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁהוּא כֵּן —
phrases.english: He said to him: If I had known that it was so,
I would not have vowed.
And רבי עקיבא allowed her again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אֲפִילּוּ אַתָּה מוֹכֵר שְׂעַר רֹאשְׁךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the man's request from step 8 and finishes the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The full כתובה must be paid even at great cost, and regret over that cost can undo the vow.

steps.title: Can movable things be taken to pay a כתובה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: a כתובה is normally paid only from land, so why did רבי עקיבא say he must sell even the hair on his head?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Are movable things tied up to pay a כתובה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and questions רבי עקיבא's words. Hair is a movable thing, but a כתובה is normally collected only from land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only the husband's land is tied up to pay the כתובה. Hair can be carried around, so it is not land. So how could רבי עקיבא say even the hair must go toward the כתובה?

keyTerms.meaning: Movable things, anything that can be carried, not land
Are tied up so the debt can be collected from them
The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: גמרא
Are movable things tied up to pay a כתובה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי עקיבא's statement in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's words that he must pay even by selling the hair on his head.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כתובה is collected only from land, so movable things like hair should not be part of the payment.

steps.title: אביי: the inheritance was land
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the father left land worth 800 דינרים, so the כתובה is paid from land.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The father left land worth eight hundred דינרים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the 800 דינרים in the story were land, not cash. So the כתובה was being paid from land, the normal way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, the man's 400 in land covers the 400 כתובה. Nothing movable has to be taken, which fits the rule from step 10.

keyTerms.meaning: Land
Worth

phrases.english: אביי said:
It was land worth eight hundred דינרים.
phrases.notes: He means the 800 the father left was land, not coins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: קַרְקַע שָׁוָה שְׁמוֹנֶה מֵאוֹת דִּינָר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the inheritance was land.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 800 was cash or movable things, which would not be tied up for a כתובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The 800 was land, so the כתובה is collected from land as usual.

steps.title: But hair is a movable thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the משנה still mentions the hair on his head, and hair is movable.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says 'the hair on his head,' and the hair on his head is a movable thing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי. Even if the inheritance was land, רבי עקיבא still spoke about selling hair, which is movable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer explains the 800 דינרים, but not the words 'hair on your head.' Those words still sound like movable things are being taken for the כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches

phrases.english: But the משנה teaches: 'the hair on his head,'
and the hair on his head is a movable thing!

steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's answer that the כתובה is paid only from land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's words about selling hair still point to movable things being used for the כתובה.

steps.title: The hair is for his own food
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains: the hair is not for the כתובה. He pays the כתובה from the land, and then he will have to sell his hair to buy food.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: Pay her from the land, even if afterward you have to sell the hair on your head to have food to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads רבי עקיבא's words. Selling the hair is not paying the כתובה. It shows how poor he will be after giving her all his land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both pieces fit together. The כתובה comes only from land, and the 'hair' line is just a picture of how little he will have left to live on.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant
And eat

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the hair as payment for the כתובה. It is what he will sell to feed himself afterward.

phrases.english: This is what he meant:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ אַתָּה מוֹכֵר שְׂעַר רֹאשְׁךָ וְאוֹכֵל.
phrases.english: Even if you then have to sell the hair on your head and eat from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ אַתָּה מוֹכֵר שְׂעַר רֹאשְׁךָ וְאוֹכֵל
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the wording of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hair is sold to pay the כתובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The land pays the כתובה, and the hair is sold afterward for his food.
steps.whatToRemember: The כתובה is paid from land. The 'hair on your head' line just shows how poor the man will be left.

steps.title: Does this prove a debtor is not left his basic needs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה proves that when a debt is collected, the debtor is not left anything to live on. רב נחמן בר רבי יצחק begins to answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you learn from here that a debtor is not left anything to live on when he pays his creditor? רב נחמן בר רבי יצחק said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to learn a rule from the story: he must pay everything, even if he has nothing left to eat. The last line names who will answer, and his answer comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a practice (סידור) of leaving a debtor some basic needs to live on, and the question is whether it applies when a creditor collects. Since רבי עקיבא made him pay everything, the גמרא wonders whether this proves no such arrangement is made. רב נחמן בר רבי יצחק will push back on this proof.
